docs.title: How isolation works
docs.text:
A child tenancy is a new tenancy OCID with its own home region. Requests signed with the child tenancy (its OCID as the first part of the Signature keyId) land in that tenancy's own, empty storage: they see none of the parent's resources, and GetTenancy reports the child's name and home region. This mirrors how floci-aws member accounts work.

A child homed in another region reaches that region by default: a request whose Host names no region (localhost:4599) lands in the signing tenancy's home region. Like any tenancy, the child can use other regions only after subscribing to them.

Organizations, organization tenancies and links are stored with the parent tenancy, so a child lists the same organization as its parent. Only the parent can update it, create more children, terminate or restore a child, or terminate a link: the same calls signed by a child are 404 NotAuthorizedOrNotFound.

docs.title: Wire notes
docs.text:
• CreateChildTenancy, UpdateOrganization, DeleteOrganizationTenancy, RestoreOrganizationTenancy and DeleteLink return 202 with an opc-work-request-id header and no body. The work request is already SUCCEEDED; for CreateChildTenancy its resources[0].identifier is the new child tenancy OCID.
  • The organizationTenancyId path parameter of DeleteOrganizationTenancy and RestoreOrganizationTenancy is the child's tenancy OCID. The parent tenancy cannot be terminated this way (400 InvalidParameter).
  • Terminating needs an ACTIVE member, restoring a DELETED one, and DeleteLink an ACTIVE link; anything else is 409 Conflict. All three honour if-match.
  • CreateSenderInvitation returns 200 with the invitation, an etag and an opc-work-request-id; CancelSenderInvitation and AcceptRecipientInvitation return 202 with an opc-work-request-id; IgnoreRecipientInvitation and both updates return the invitation with an etag. Invitation lists are wrapped and take the SDK's status and lifecycleState enums; ListRecipientInvitations has no limit or sort, as in the SDK.
  • ListLinks rejects a lifecycleState outside CREATING, ACTIVE, INACTIVE, UPDATING, FAILED, TERMINATED with 400 InvalidParameter.
  • Lists are wrapped ({"items":[…]}) and paged with opc-next-page.
  • GetOrganization, GetOrganizationTenancy and GetLink return an etag; UpdateOrganization honours if-match.
  • homeRegion must be a region the parent tenancy is subscribed to (its home region, or one added with CreateRegionSubscription); otherwise the request fails with 400 InvalidParameter.
  • compartmentId on CreateChildTenancy and ListOrganizations must be the caller's own tenancy; another tenancy is 404 NotAuthorizedOrNotFound.
  • A CORE link is always created, plus one link per entry in features.

docs.title: Emulator choices
docs.text:
The OCI SDKs leave these open, so floci-oci picks:

  • Organizations data is global. Real OCI serves this API on a regional host and does not say whether its data is shared across regions; floci-oci keeps organizations, organization tenancies, links and their work requests tenancy-wide, like Identity, so every region of the tenancy sees the same organization.
  • homeRegion accepts a region name (us-phoenix-1) or a region key (PHX).
  • governanceStatus defaults to OPTED_IN when omitted.
  • Organizations and links get global OCIDs: ocid1.organization.<realm>..… and ocid1.link.<realm>..…. A child tenancy's OCID uses the realm of its home region.
  • When no subscriptionId is given, the organization's default subscription is the parent tenancy's own subscription (see Subscriptions below).
  • The child tenancy limit is not enforced. Oracle's child-tenancy-count limit defaults to 0 in every tenancy (service limits, Organizations), so a tenancy needs it raised before its first child; floci-oci behaves as a tenancy whose limit has been raised, and creates any number of children.
  • A new child starts with an administrator. The SDK only says that policyName names "the administrator policy in the child tenancy". floci-oci seeds the child's IAM with an Administrators group, a user named after adminEmail (also its email) in that group, and a policy named policyName (Tenant_Admin_Policy when omitted) with the single statement ALLOW GROUP Administrators to manage all-resources IN TENANCY. Requests signed with the child see them; policies are stored, not evaluated. A tenancy that joins through an invitation already exists and is not seeded.
  • Termination is immediate and reversible. DeleteOrganizationTenancy moves the member to DELETED with timeLeft set and terminates its active links, under the work request type TERMINATE_ORGANIZATION_TENANCY. The child tenancy stays registered and its data is kept, so requests signed with it still work. RestoreOrganizationTenancy (RESTORE_TENANCY) makes it ACTIVE again and reactivates the links its termination ended, but not links terminated on their own before. Real OCI does not document the termination lifecycle or how long a terminated tenancy stays restorable.

  • DeleteLink moves the link to TERMINATED with timeTerminated set (TERMINATE_LINK), for any feature, CORE included; the child stays a member of the organization.

  • AddGovernance and RemoveGovernance set a member's governanceStatus to OPTED_IN or OPTED_OUT. The parent or the member itself may call them; asking for the status a member already has is 409 Conflict; the member must be an ACTIVE child (the parent is 400 InvalidParameter). Their work requests use the types SELF_OPT_IN and SELF_OPT_OUT, the closest values in the SDK enum (it names no add or remove type). Only members OPTED_IN are governed by the parent's governance rules.

  • ApproveOrganizationTenancyForTransfer and UnapproveOrganizationTenancyForTransfer take the parent tenancy as compartmentId (mandatory, as in the SDK) and return the organization tenancy with an etag, synchronously, with isApprovedForTransfer set or cleared. Only the parent may call them, on an ACTIVE child; asking for the flag the member already has is 409 Conflict. The SDKs do not say who approves a transfer; floci-oci makes it the parent, like every other change to a member. Nothing moves the approved tenancy yet.

  • ListLinkFeatures returns CORE, which every link carries (the one feature the SDK names), followed by each other feature on an ACTIVE link of the caller's organization. The SDK request has no page or limit, so the list is never paged: every feature comes back at once. Display names repeat the feature; the SDK fixes no catalogue of features or their descriptions.

docs.title: Invitations
docs.text:
The SDKs give the shapes but not the flow, so floci-oci picks:

  • The recipient invitation is delivered at once, with its own OCID (ocid1.recipientinvitation…, the sender's is ocid1.senderinvitation…); each points at the other. Both start ACTIVE with status PENDING, and subjects defaults to LINK.
  • Only a tenancy that is not a child can invite (404 otherwise), and only a tenancy outside any organization can be invited or accept (409 Conflict). A second pending invitation to the same tenancy is also 409 Conflict; inviting yourself is 400 InvalidParameter.
  • Accepting makes the recipient a child of the sender: it joins the sender's organization (created if needed) with a CORE link plus one link per invitation feature, and both invitations become ACCEPTED.
  • Ignoring marks the recipient's side IGNORED. The sender's side stays PENDING, since its status enum has no ignored value, until the sender cancels it.
  • Cancel, accept and ignore need a PENDING invitation (409 Conflict otherwise). Accepting is also 409 Conflict when the recipient has joined another organization, or the sender has become a child, since the invitation was sent.
  • An invitation without displayName uses its own OCID as the name, because the summary shape requires one.

docs.title: Domains
docs.text:
The SDKs give the shapes and the status enum, but not the verification flow, so floci-oci picks:

  • A claim is verified at once. floci-oci cannot see DNS, so CreateDomain returns the domain ACTIVE with status ACTIVE. It still issues a txtRecord (oci-domain-verification=…) of the kind the owner would add to their DNS. The work request is REGISTER_DOMAIN. Domain names are stored lower-cased.
  • A domain name can be claimed by one tenancy at a time: another claim of an ACTIVE domain is 409 Conflict, whichever tenancy holds it.
  • DeleteDomain releases the domain: it answers 204 (the SDK returns no work request), and the record stays readable with lifecycleState DELETED and status RELEASED, which is what the OCI CLI polls for. The name can then be claimed again, and the domain's governance becomes INACTIVE. UpdateDomain changes only the tags, as in the SDK.
  • A domain has at most one ACTIVE governance (409 Conflict otherwise). Its ONS topic and subscription OCIDs are stored as given, unchecked (floci-oci has no Notifications service), and isGovernanceEnabled starts true. DeleteDomainGovernance answers 204 and leaves the record INACTIVE. Governance is recorded, not enforced.
  • isGovernanceEnabled and subscriptionEmail on CreateDomain are accepted; the Domain shape returns neither.
  • Domains and their governance are visible only to the tenancy that claimed them. Changing a released domain or an inactive governance is 409 Conflict.

docs.title: Subscriptions
docs.text:
Subscriptions are billing records held in Oracle's commerce systems, which floci-oci does not have, so it models the minimum the API needs:

  • Every tenancy owns one subscription, a V2 (cloud) subscription: entityVersion V2, service CLOUDCM, currency USD, ACTIVE. Its OCID is derived from the tenancy OCID, so it is the same on every call and needs no stored record. ListSubscriptions returns it (and nothing for entityVersion=V1); GetSubscription only for the tenancy that owns it.
  • Assigned subscriptions are the ones a tenancy consumes: those mapped to it and, for a child with no mapping, its organization's default subscription, as the SDK describes ("any tenancy joining the organization will automatically get assigned this subscription"). An assigned subscription keeps the id of the subscription it is.
  • A subscription mapping assigns the caller's own subscription to the caller or to an ACTIVE child of its organization (404 for any other tenancy, 409 Conflict for a second active mapping of the same pair). It is synchronous, isExplicitlyAssigned true. DeleteSubscriptionMapping answers 204 and keeps the mapping readable as DELETED with timeTerminated, as Terraform's oci_tenantmanagercontrolplane_subscription_mapping reads it.
  • Each subscription has one synthetic line item (PAYGO, ten years from the tenancy's creation), and its available regions are the regions of the tenancy's realm.
  • A mapping to a child ends (DELETED, timeTerminated set) when the child stops being an ACTIVE member, for example when it is terminated.
  • A defaultUcmSubscriptionId set through UpdateOrganization or CreateChildTenancy that is not a tenancy's own subscription is still what children consume, but no tenancy owns it: it has no line items or available regions, and it cannot be mapped.
  • Subscriptions have no stored record, so their etag is derived from the returned shape. A subscription's dates are its owning tenancy's creation time.

docs.title: Orders
docs.text:
An activation token is a JWT (RFC 7519) issued by Oracle's order system, which floci-oci does not have:

  • Any well-formed JWT (a JSON object header, a JSON object payload and a signature) is accepted, and its signature is not checked (floci-oci never checks request signatures either); anything else is 400 InvalidParameter. The text claims orderNumber, adminEmail and dataCenterRegion and the numeric iat (the subscription start) are used when present. When they are not, orderNumber and the subscription's spmSubscriptionId are derived from the token, so the same token always names the same order; adminEmail is admin@example.com; the subscription starts at the epoch; and dataCenterRegion is left out.
  • orderState is PENDING until the order is activated, then ACTIVATED. The SDK gives the field no enum, so both values are floci-oci's.
  • ActivateOrder activates the order into the caller's tenancy, which must be the body's compartmentId. It returns 202 with an opc-work-request-id (type ACTIVATE_ORDER_EXISTING_TENANCY; the SDK enum also has COMPLETE_ORDER_ACTIVATION, but this call activates into an existing tenancy), once per token; a second activation is 409 Conflict. Activation records the order and changes nothing else.

docs.title: Remaining gaps
docs.text: Work-request errors and logs are always empty, since every Organizations work request finishes SUCCEEDED when it is returned. The child tenancy limit is not enforced (see above).

oci organizations child-tenancy create $E --compartment-id "$TENANCY" \

oci organizations organization list $E --compartment-id "$TENANCY"
oci organizations link list $E

docs.title: Database with PostgreSQL
docs.text: OCI Database with PostgreSQL, API version 20220915 (SDK package psql, client PostgresqlClient, CLI oci psql). Each DB system is backed by a real PostgreSQL container, so the endpoint and certificate returned by GetConnectionDetails are ones an application can connect to. Real OCI serves the API on postgresql.{region}.oci.{domain}; floci-oci serves it on port 4599 with the other services.

docs.title: How a DB system runs
docs.text:
• One container per DB system. CreateDbSystem returns the system CREATING with an IN_PROGRESS work request and starts a postgres:<major>-alpine container in the background. Once PostgreSQL accepts connections the system becomes ACTIVE and the work request SUCCEEDED, which is what Terraform and oci psql db-system create --wait-for-state wait on. A container that exits, or one that is not ready within FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_PSQL_READY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (default 120), marks both FAILED, and the reason is listed by ListWorkRequestErrors.
  • Version and image. dbVersion takes a major (15) or a major and minor (15.8); its major picks the image through FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_PSQL_IMAGE (default postgres:{major}-alpine). Once the server is up, dbVersion reports the server's own version, such as 15.8.
  • Endpoint. PostgreSQL's port is published on a host port from FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_PSQL_BASE_PORT..MAX_PORT (default 15432..15531), one per DB system. GetConnectionDetails returns localhost and that port when floci-oci runs on the host. When floci-oci runs in a container it returns the PostgreSQL container's name and port 5432, for clients on the same Docker network; set FLOCI_OCI_DOCKER_ENDPOINT_MODE=published to get the Docker host and the published port instead, for clients on the host.
  • TLS. Every DB system has its own self-signed certificate, returned as caCertificate. PostgreSQL serves it, so sslmode=verify-full works with that file as sslrootcert. Unencrypted connections are accepted too.
  • Credentials. The admin user and password come from credentials (PLAIN_TEXT, or VAULT_SECRET read from a secret in floci-oci's own Vault). As on real OCI the password is never returned, and floci-oci does not store it either. ResetMasterUserPassword changes it in the running database.
  • Stop, start, restart. StopDbSystem removes the container and keeps the data volume (INACTIVE); StartDbSystem and RestartDbInstanceInDbSystem bring it back with the same data, and the same host port when it is still free.
  • Delete. DeleteDbSystem removes the container. The DB system stays readable as DELETED, as on real OCI, since clients poll it to see the delete finish. The data volume is removed in memory storage mode or when prune-volumes-on-delete is set, like the other sidecars.
  • Mock mode. FLOCI_OCI_SERVICES_PSQL_MOCK=true starts no container: every DB system is ACTIVE at once and every operation completes immediately, with nothing listening on the endpoint. Useful where Docker is not available.
  • Teardown. Containers are stopped on shutdown and removed, with their volumes, by POST /_floci-oci/state/reset, whatever prune-volumes-on-delete says. After a restart of floci-oci with persistent storage, the DB systems that were ACTIVE are started again. An operation the restart interrupted is settled first: a delete finishes, a create ends FAILED (its master password was never stored), and a stop, restart or password reset fails its work request, leaving the system ACTIVE as it was.

docs.title: Wire notes
docs.text:
• CreateDbSystem returns 200 with the DB system, an etag and opc-work-request-id. Every other mutation returns 202 with opc-work-request-id and no body.
  • Lists are wrapped ({"items":[…]}) and paged with opc-next-page.
  • shape accepts what Terraform sends (PostgreSQL.VM.Standard.E4.Flex.2.32GB, or PostgreSQL.VM.Standard.E4.Flex with instanceOcpuCount and instanceMemorySizeInGBs) and the bare shape. The response carries the bare shape and both sizes.
  • storageDetails.availabilityDomain is required when isRegionallyDurable is false and rejected when it is true (400 InvalidParameter).
  • Operations need the right state: StartDbSystem an INACTIVE system, the others an ACTIVE one. Otherwise they return 409 IncorrectState.
  • compartmentId must be an existing compartment or the tenancy, and the request must be sent to a region the tenancy is subscribed to, like every other regional service.

docs.title: Emulator choices
docs.text:
OCI's SDKs leave these open, so floci-oci picks:

  • Versions and shapes. Majors 14 and 15 and shapes VM.Standard.E4.Flex and VM.Standard.E5.Flex are the ones Oracle's Terraform examples use. 16 and 17 are accepted as well so newer versions can be tried. Anything else is 400 InvalidParameter.
  • OCIDs. ocid1.postgresqldbsystem…, ocid1.postgresqldbinstance… and ocid1.postgresqldefaultconfiguration…. A default configuration OCID is the same on every start.
  • Default configurations. Each version has a flexible one and a fixed one per shape and size. A DB system created with a sized shape (PostgreSQL.VM.Standard.E4.Flex.2.32GB) gets the fixed configuration for that size, and one created with a bare shape and separate sizes gets the flexible one, which is what Terraform needs to show no changes on the next plan.
  • Work requests. The resource entity type is postgresqlDbSystem. Start, stop, restart and password reset report UPDATE_POSTGRESQL_DB_SYSTEM, since the API has no value of their own. Backups use postgresqlBackup and the *_POSTGRESQL_DB_SYSTEM_BACKUP types; a copy reports CREATE_POSTGRESQL_DB_SYSTEM_BACKUP and a restore UPDATE_POSTGRESQL_DB_SYSTEM.
  • credentials is required on create, because only a fresh DB system can be created.
  • Several instances are one database. instanceCount above 1 gives that many instance records, all served by the one container (see Instances and replicas).
  • Defaults. When omitted: 2 OCPUs and 32 GB, 75000 IOPS, maintenance window SUN 00:00, backup policy NONE, and the default configuration for the version.
  • Network. subnetId and nsgIds are stored unchecked, since there is no networking service.
  • Update is metadata only, except the configuration. Shape, sizes, IOPS and management policy change what the API reports, not the running container. A new configId does reach PostgreSQL (see Custom configurations).

docs.title: Custom configurations
docs.text:
A configuration overrides PostgreSQL settings for one major version and shape. As in the SDK, every configuration call is synchronous: create, get and update return the Configuration with an etag; delete and change-compartment answer 204 with no work request.

  • Settings. OCI publishes no list of the settings a configuration may override, so floci-oci serves a small one: work_mem, maintenance_work_mem, effective_io_concurrency, random_page_cost, log_min_duration_statement, statement_timeout (applied with a reload), and max_connections and shared_buffers (need a restart). Any other key in dbConfigurationOverrides is 400 InvalidParameter. Both default and custom configurations report these as configurationDetails.items, with defaults, allowed values and isRestartRequired.
  • Shape. A configuration with no shape (or shape PostgreSQL) fits every shape and reports shape PostgreSQL and sizes 0, the SDK's multi-shape case. A flexible one for a named shape keeps that shape with sizes 0, which is what Terraform reads back. A fixed one takes its size from a sized shape (VM.Standard.E4.Flex.4.64GB) or from instanceOcpuCount and instanceMemorySizeInGBs. Custom OCIDs are ocid1.postgresqlconfiguration…: they never contain defaultconfiguration, the substring Terraform uses to tell a default configuration from a custom one.
  • Applying it. A DB system created with a configId starts with its settings: the restart-only ones on the postgres command line, the others with ALTER SYSTEM once the server accepts connections. UpdateDbSystem with dbConfigurationParams puts a new configuration into effect: applyConfig RESTART restarts the container (UPDATING, then ACTIVE), and RELOAD (Terraform's default) reloads the settings that allow it and leaves the restart-only ones for the next start, as PostgreSQL does. A value PostgreSQL rejects on RELOAD fails the work request; the system stays ACTIVE with its previous configuration. A value that keeps PostgreSQL from starting leaves the system NEEDS_ATTENTION: UpdateDbSystem with another configuration restarts it with that one, and StartDbSystem tries the same one again. OCI documents neither path, so both are floci-oci's choice. In mock mode the configuration is only recorded.
  • Lifecycle. A configuration is ACTIVE at once (the SDK has no CREATING state). Deleting it leaves it readable as DELETED; deleting one a DB system that is not DELETED still uses is 409 Conflict. Only the names, description, compatible shapes and tags can be updated.
  • Listing. ListConfigurations lists custom configurations only: configType DEFAULT or COPIED gives an empty list. Default configurations are served by ListDefaultConfigurations.
  • Limit. 20 configurations that are not DELETED per tenancy per region, Oracle's service limit; the 21st is 400 LimitExceeded.

docs.title: Backups and recovery
docs.text:
A backup is a pg_dumpall of the running DB system: every database and role, without role passwords. Dumps are kept by the emulator, under psql-backups in its persistent path, or in a temporary directory with memory storage, and not in any DB system container: the admin of a DB system is a PostgreSQL superuser who can read any file its container can see. A dump is copied into a container only while it loads there, and removed afterwards. The temporary directory is removed when the emulator stops.

  • Create. CreateBackup needs an ACTIVE DB system and answers 202 with a work request. The backup is CREATING while the dump runs in the background, then ACTIVE with backupSize in whole gigabytes (at least 1), or FAILED with the error in lifecycleDetails and on the work request. A backup the emulator's restart interrupted is FAILED too. sourceType is MANUAL. In mock mode the backup is ACTIVE at once and holds no data.
  • Restore. RestoreDbSystem with a backupId replaces the DB system's databases with the backup, in place: every database is dropped (closing its connections) and the dump is loaded. Roles are kept, so the admin password stays the current one. A DB system created with source BACKUP starts empty and loads the backup before it turns ACTIVE, with the credentials of its create request. Any SQL error stops the load: the only statement skipped is CREATE ROLE for a role the DB system already has. A failed load leaves the DB system NEEDS_ATTENTION (FAILED on create), and its old databases are already gone by then; StartDbSystem brings it back, and another restore can run. The backup must be ACTIVE, in the same tenancy and region, and of the same major version. The ad of a restore is accepted and ignored, since every instance runs in the one container.
  • Point in time. floci-oci archives no WAL, so a timeToRestore (on RestoreDbSystem, or a POINT_IN_TIME_DB_SYSTEM source) resolves to the newest ACTIVE backup of that DB system whose data was taken at or before it, so a copy counts from its source's time, not its own; with none it is 400 InvalidParameter. GetPitrDetails is ACTIVE when the management policy has pitrPolicy.kind STANDARD, with one recovery window from the first backup until now, and INACTIVE otherwise.
  • Copy. BackupCopy creates a COPIED backup in each requested region of the tenancy, at once, sharing the source's dump, and records it in the source's copyStatus. If any region would go over the limit, it is 400 LimitExceeded and no copy is made.
  • Delete. The backup stays readable as DELETED. Its dump stays until a state reset (POST /_floci-oci/state/reset) removes the dumps.
  • Schedules. The backupPolicy of a management policy is stored and returned, but no scheduled backup is ever taken. retentionPeriod is stored, and nothing expires.
  • Limit. 10 backups that are not DELETED per tenancy per region, Oracle's service limit; the 11th is 400 LimitExceeded.

docs.title: Instances and replicas
docs.text:
Instances and replicas are tracked by the management plane only: every instance of a DB system is served by its one PostgreSQL container, and a replica is a DB system with its own container and no replication from its primary. Every operation here finishes at once, with a SUCCEEDED UPDATE_POSTGRESQL_DB_SYSTEM work request.

  • PatchDbSystem takes INSERT at selection instances with a CreateDbInstanceDetails value, and REMOVE at instances[?id == '<id>'], the selections Terraform sends, and updates instanceCount. Any other operation or selection is 400 InvalidParameter, removing the last instance too. An empty patch succeeds.
  • FailoverDbSystem makes another instance the primary one, the one GetPrimaryDbInstance returns: dbInstanceId if given, else the first standby in ad, else the first standby. A DB system with one instance is 409 Conflict.
  • Replicas. A DB system created with source DB_SYSTEM is a WARM_STANDBY_DB_SYSTEM and its primary becomes PRIMARY_DB_SYSTEM. The primary must be ACTIVE, in the same tenancy (any region), not itself a replica, and of the same major version. A replica may leave out credentials: it takes the primary's admin username and a password nobody knows, since floci-oci keeps no password; set one with ResetMasterUserPassword. ListDbSystemReplicas lists the replicas that are not being deleted.
  • Roles. SwitchOver, called on the primary, swaps it with the named replica; the other replicas follow the new primary. ChangeRoleToReplica makes a standalone DB system a replica, and ChangeRoleToStandalone detaches one (both change modes do the same). A primary with no replica left, after a role change or a delete, is standalone again. Deleting a primary that still has replicas is 409 Conflict. A role change on a DB system in the wrong role is 409 Conflict.
  • replicationConfig is stored and returned. Both fields are mandatory in the response, so one never set reads as isRpoEnforced false and rpoInSeconds 0.

docs.title: Kerberos and insights
docs.text:
Both are recorded and returned exactly as sent; neither changes the running PostgreSQL.

  • kerberosAuthDetails is set by UpdateDbSystem only, as in the SDK. ENABLED needs at least one entry in credentials (realmName, keytabSecretId, keytabSecretVersion), and each keytab must be an existing Vault secret version, else 400 RelatedResourceNotAuthorizedOrNotFound. PostgreSQL is not configured for GSSAPI.
  • odspInsightDetails is set on create or update. ENABLED takes an odspInsightList whose insightType is QUERY_INSIGHT, the only type the SDK defines. No insight data is collected.
  • ListInsightCapabilities reports QUERY_INSIGHT with the AAS_TIME_SERIES and TOP_QUERIES data types. OCI documents the enum values only, so the descriptions and units are floci-oci's.

docs.title: Service limits
docs.text: Oracle's limits for the service, per tenancy per region, are enforced: 8 DB systems, 10 backups and 20 configurations, counting each that is not DELETED. The one past the limit is 400 LimitExceeded.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
E="--endpoint http://localhost:4599"
TENANCY=ocid1.tenancy.oc1..flocilocaltenancy0000000000000000000000000000000000000000

# Create a DB system and wait for it
ID=$(oci psql db-system create $E --compartment-id "$TENANCY" --display-name demo-db \
  --db-version 16 --shape PostgreSQL.VM.Standard.E4.Flex.2.32GB \
  --network-details '{"subnetId":"ocid1.subnet.oc1.iad.demo"}' \
  --storage-details '{"systemType":"OCI_OPTIMIZED_STORAGE","isRegionallyDurable":true}' \
  --credentials '{"username":"admin_user","passwordDetails":{"passwordType":"PLAIN_TEXT","password":"BEstrO0ng_#11"}}' \
  --wait-for-state SUCCEEDED --query 'data.resources[0].identifier' --raw-output)

# Where to connect, and the certificate to trust
oci psql connection-details get $E --db-system-id "$ID" > connection.json
jq -r '.data."ca-certificate"' connection.json > ca.pem
PORT=$(jq -r '.data."primary-db-endpoint".port' connection.json)

psql "host=localhost port=$PORT dbname=postgres user=admin_user sslmode=verify-full sslrootcert=ca.pem"

docs.title: Queue
docs.text: OCI Queue — API version 20210201. Control plane and data plane are both served on port 4599; the queue's messagesEndpoint points back at the emulator.

docs.title: Supported operations
docs.text: Area Operations Queues CreateQueue, GetQueue, ListQueues, UpdateQueue, DeleteQueue, ChangeCompartment, PurgeQueue Messages PutMessages, GetMessages, DeleteMessage(s), UpdateMessage(s) Observability GetStats, ListChannels Work requests Get, List, errors, logs (/20210201/workRequests)

docs.title: Wire notes
docs.text:
• Every control-plane mutation is work-request driven: 202 with an opc-work-request-id header and no body. Poll GetWorkRequest — the emulator records the queue OCID in resources[] and sets timeFinished immediately, which is what Terraform's retry predicate requires.
  • Lists are wrapped — {"items":[…]} — unlike Identity's bare arrays.
  • sortBy values are camelCase (timeCreated, displayName), not the SCREAMING_CASE KMS uses.
  • retentionInSeconds is set at create time and is not updatable.

docs.title: Message semantics
docs.text:
• visibilityInSeconds defaults to the queue's setting; 0 is a peek — the message stays visible but its deliveryCount still increments.
  • timeoutInSeconds > 0 long-polls until a message arrives (capped at 10s in the emulator); 0 short-polls.
  • With deadLetterQueueDeliveryCount > 0, over-delivered messages move to the DLQ and show up under dlq in GetStats.
  • Messages expire after retentionInSeconds.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
E="--endpoint http://localhost:4599"
TENANCY=ocid1.tenancy.oc1..flocilocaltenancy0000000000000000000000000000000000000000

oci queue queue create $E --compartment-id "$TENANCY" --display-name demo
oci queue messages put-messages $E --queue-id <queueId> \
  --messages '[{"content":"hello queue"}]'
oci queue messages get-messages $E --queue-id <queueId>

docs.title: Notes & limitations
docs.text: Consumer groups, channel consumption limits and per-channel purge filters beyond channelIds are not implemented.

docs.title: Streaming
docs.text: OCI Streaming — API version 20180418. Kafka-like partitioned append-only logs with cursor-based consumption.

docs.title: Supported operations
docs.text: Area Operations Streams CreateStream, GetStream, ListStreams, UpdateStream, DeleteStream Produce PutMessages Consume CreateCursor, CreateGroupCursor, GetMessages Groups ConsumerCommit, ConsumerHeartbeat, GetGroup, UpdateGroup Work requests Get, List, errors, logs (/20180418/workRequests)

docs.title: Wire notes
docs.text:
• CreateStream is dual-mode: it returns the full Stream body and an opc-work-request-id header. Terraform waits on the work request and reads the stream OCID from its resources[] (entityType containing stream, actionType CREATED).
  • Lists are bare JSON arrays. retentionInHours is on Stream but not on StreamSummary, so it only appears on Get.
  • GetMessages takes a mandatory cursor query parameter, returns a bare array and advances through the opc-next-cursor response header.
  • Message key and value are base64; Message.stream carries the stream name, not its OCID.
  • Commit and heartbeat are POSTs with the cursor in the query string and an empty body.

docs.title: Partitioning and cursors
docs.text:
• Messages with a key hash to a stable partition; keyless messages round-robin.
  • Cursor types: TRIM_HORIZON, LATEST, AT_OFFSET, AFTER_OFFSET, AT_TIME. Group cursors support only TRIM_HORIZON, LATEST, AT_TIME.
  • Cursors are opaque (base64) and bound to their stream — using one against another stream is a 400.
  • Committing a group cursor persists per-partition offsets; a fresh group cursor for the same group resumes from them.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
E="--endpoint http://localhost:4599"
TENANCY=ocid1.tenancy.oc1..flocilocaltenancy0000000000000000000000000000000000000000

oci streaming admin stream create $E --compartment-id "$TENANCY" \
  --name demo-stream --partitions 2

docs.title: Notes & limitations
docs.text: Stream pools are synthesized (a pool OCID is minted per stream) and their Kafka connection settings, connect harnesses and the archiver are not implemented.
